sections.h2: Where is the Gladwin County Register of Deeds?
sections.html:
The Gladwin County Register of Deeds is at 401 West Cedar Avenue in the city of Gladwin, the same building that houses the county's commission chambers, and it is open Monday to Friday from 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. Anyone recording a deed, mortgage discharge or lien for land in the county does it there.

ItemGladwin County Register of Deeds
Address401 W Cedar Ave, Gladwin, MI 48624
Telephone989-426-7551
HoursMonday to Friday, 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m.
Recording fee$30 per document, any number of pages
Extra instruments assigned or discharged$3 each, on top of the $30
Certify a recorded document$5
Copies$1 per page
Search by year50 cents a year, $5 minimum

Source: Gladwin County Register of Deeds page. The flat $30 already includes the state remonumentation and automation fees.

sections.h2: Can you record or search Gladwin County documents online?
sections.html:
Yes, in part. The county's register page offers an online land records search and a free fraud alert sign-up, and it says the office takes e-recording through three vendors. Paper documents can be brought in or mailed.

The office also does passport work that has nothing to do with real estate. It processes new passport applications by appointment, keeps renewal forms on hand, and takes passport photos for $10. If you are coming in for a deed and a passport on the same trip, call first.

A fraud alert suits anyone who owns land they do not live on. The 2020 census found 34.7% of the county's 16,862 housing units vacant, and an owner who is rarely on site is the one least likely to notice a document recorded against the parcel.

sections.h2: What does Gladwin County charge when a deed is recorded?
sections.html:
The recording fee is $30 whether the deed is one page or twenty, so the cost of recording rarely changes the size of a sale. The money bill that does change is transfer tax, which is based on price.

The county page cites MCL 600.2567 for its fees, and the statute matches the figures in the table above: $3 for each extra instrument in an assignment or discharge, $5 to certify, $1 a page for copies and 50 cents per year searched, with a $5 floor. A document must be paid for when it is left for recording, except an electronic filing, which can be paid within one business day.

  • State transfer tax: $3.75 for each $500 of value.
  • County transfer tax: 55 cents for each $500, the rate for counties under two million people.
  • Who pays: the seller, to the county treasurer, within 15 days after the deed is delivered.
  • On a $100,000 sale: 200 units of $500, so $750 state tax and $110 county tax.

The deed has to state its value on its face, or carry an affidavit of value. Transfers to a child or grandchild, deeds in foreclosure and mortgages are exempt from the state tax.

sections.h2: What is Gladwin County like for a house seller?
sections.html:
Gladwin County is a rural, low-density county in the middle of Michigan's Lower Peninsula, with about 26,077 residents in the Census Bureau's 2025 estimate. It was set off in 1831 and organized in 1875, and it takes its name from the British commandant at Detroit during Pontiac's War in 1763.

The county covers 502 square miles of land, and most of the Tittabawassee River's water comes from within its borders. M-18 runs along the western side and through the cities of Gladwin and Beaverton, M-30 passes through the center, and M-61 runs east to west through Gladwin and White Star. Seven counties border it: Ogemaw, Arenac, Bay, Midland, Clare, Isabella and Roscommon. The county has two cities, Gladwin and Beaverton, and 15 townships.

  • Housing: 17,329 housing units and 11,280 households, with 86.1% of homes owner-occupied.
  • Value: a median owner-occupied home is worth $162,300, with median gross rent of $690.
  • Age: 28.9% of residents are 65 or older.
  • Income: median household income is $55,349.
  • Building: 93 building permits were issued in 2025.

Source: Census QuickFacts.

sections.h2: How does Gladwin County property tax affect a sale?
sections.html:
Tax for the year is billed by the township or city treasurer and collected by the county only after it turns delinquent. Summer tax is billed on July 1 and payable without interest by September 14, and winter tax is billed on December 1 and payable by February 14. The treasurer's page makes an exception for Gladwin City on the summer date.

Anything unpaid on March 1 goes to the Gladwin County Treasurer with a 4% fee and 1% monthly interest. The county's timeline lists a $15 certified mailing fee on October 1, forfeiture on the following March 1, a personal visit fee and a publication fee in the summer and fall, and a final payment date of March 31 after which title passes to the county. The treasurer's page states that postmarks do not count for payment dates, since the payment date is the day the office receives and processes it.

The county treasurer's office certifies deeds, plat maps and tax histories, so ask it for a payoff and tax history before a sale. For the principal residence exemption, taxable value and hardship or veteran exemptions, the page sends owners to the township or city assessor. Parcels that finish foreclosure are auctioned at tax-sale.info.

sections.h2: Who checks assessments in Gladwin County?
sections.html:
The county equalization department checks them. Its page says the department surveys local assessments for the Board of Commissioners and must make sure each class of property in each local unit is assessed between 49% and 50% of true cash value, based on an annual study. The local assessor remains responsible for fairness between individual parcels.

  • April: the equalization report of values for each class in each local unit.
  • June: millage reduction fractions for each taxing authority.
  • October: the apportionment report of millage rates the county may levy.
  • December 31: the equalization study of sales and appraisals.

The department also keeps the countywide database of values, property descriptions, title changes, owner names and addresses, and exemption status. It runs a GIS viewer for locating land records and publishes principal residence exemption forms. A deed recorded at the register's office shows up there as a title change, which is why a buyer should send in a change of address form after closing.

sections.h2: What if a seller cannot clear the tax before closing?
sections.html:
A sale can still close, since the title company pays the delinquent amount from the proceeds. The treasurer's payoff includes the fees and interest that have built up to the day of closing.

Timing matters because costs step up. The county's timeline shows a $15 mailing fee in October, a forfeiture fee on the next March 1 when interest rises from 1% to 1.5% a month retroactive to the original delinquency date, then a personal visit fee and a publication fee. All redemption rights end at the close of business on March 31, so a seller who is close to that date should get a payoff figure first. A cash buyer who purchases as-is can often close on a short timeline when repairs or an inheritance are holding up a regular listing. Gladwin's own treasurer page is the place to read for current local fee amounts.

faqs.q: What is the recording fee in Gladwin County?
faqs.a: The fee is a flat $30 per document, regardless of the number of pages. It includes the state remonumentation and automation fees, and an additional $3 applies for each extra instrument assigned or discharged in one document.

faqs.q: What are the hours of the Gladwin County Register of Deeds?
faqs.a: The office is open Monday to Friday from 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. at 401 West Cedar Avenue in Gladwin. The telephone number on the county page is 989-426-7551.

faqs.q: Does the Gladwin County Register of Deeds accept e-recording?
faqs.a: Yes. The county's page says the office offers e-recording through three vendors. Ask the office which vendors it uses before you send a document electronically.

faqs.q: Who pays transfer tax on a Gladwin County sale?
faqs.a: The seller pays. The state charges $3.75 per $500 and the county 55 cents per $500, and the payment goes to the county treasurer within 15 days after the deed is delivered.

faqs.q: When does unpaid Gladwin County property tax become delinquent?
faqs.a: It turns delinquent on March 1 of the following year, when the township or city returns it to the county treasurer. A 4% administration fee and 1% monthly interest are added from that date.
